object_description: compact five-storey volume set perpendicular to the slope on terraced ground
design_condition: the compact volume is placed perpendicular to the slope and set back from the road, completing the ensemble while its small footprint frees terraced open space and lets cold air flow towards the city

positive: The compact volume completes the ensemble of the school complex
Precise positioning of the five-storey building blends in with the existing context
Front zones and square areas achieve particularly good integration into the neighbouring and superordinate environment
The compact positioning perpendicular to the slope takes special consideration of the listed building
Cold air flows can pass more freely than today towards the city centre
The small footprint allows optimised, diversely usable outdoor spaces
Setting the building back from the road creates a relaxed spatial entrance situation
It opens up great potential for different, even small-scale uses of the terraces
Efficient access allows different entrances and thus the maximum possible scope for use
The spatial arrangement of the communal ground floor uses is correct
The upper floors offer a very flexible spatial concept promoting collaborative and individual learning
Each cluster has its own access and rooms can be flexibly divided around the central area
The compact layout enables optimum separation of uses and operating units at different times
The external appearance is light due to its horizontality
Striking suspended canopies shape the expression and work as shading without restricting the view out
The large floor area does not have a negative impact on the overall economy
Convincing in urban setting, functionality and integration into the overall complex
The compactness offers generous outdoor spaces valuable to school and neighbourhood
Consistent separation of areas offers a high degree of flexibility of use
negative: Using the central terrace for the two sports fields leaves the canteen and entrance area without a usable apron
Large contiguous sealed areas have an unfavourable effect on the microclimatic situation
A slightly more relaxed arrangement of the different uses still needs to be explored
The proposed spatial separation by sliding walls does not appear practicable in operation
The food serving area in connection with the kitchen still needs optimisation
The austerity of the surrounding design should be given more lightness overall
